events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Why, hello there, everyone! Clara Bellingham, at your service! Oh my stars, what a perfectly magnificent foyer — dusty as Aunt Mabel's attic, but magnificent all the same! Now, I do believe a proper lady always signs the guest book upon arrival. Let me just have a little peek at this darlin' thing and see who else has graced these halls before us. After all, the Doily Diamond isn't going to find itself, and every little clue counts!

Oh, I am just tickled pink to be here! A real mystery in a real mansion! Now, that chandelier up there looks like it could fall at any moment, but I'm sure it's perfectly fine. And Dick Dastardly and Sneekly in the same room? I'm sure they're both just the sweetest gentlemen. Let's see what this guest book tells us!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome to Doily Manor, everyone! I am Pemberton, the estate manager. Do make yourselves at home — though I must warn you, the old place has a few... quirks. Now then, let me just check the guest book here — one must keep proper records, you understand.

So many guests milling about, and yet no sign of Clara Bellingham. She must be deeper in the manor already — blast the woman, she's always one step ahead. I need to find her before she stumbles onto anything valuable. But first, let me play the dutiful estate manager and gather intelligence. Every good scheme begins with reconnaissance, and every GREAT scheme begins with an overly elaborate reconnaissance plan involving at least three contingencies and a backup disguise.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right, lads, we've arrived! Doily Manor — look at the state of it! That chandelier's one sneeze away from turning someone into a pancake, I'm tellin' ya. Now listen, Clara's somewhere in this house and we ain't leaving till we know she's safe. First things first — let's see who's been signing in at this old guest book. Knowledge is power, boys, knowledge is power!

Something about that Sneekly fella... the way he's standing there all casual-like. Too casual. Like a cat what's already eaten the canary but wants you to think it's been on a diet. Can't say nothing though — Danny don't accuse without proof. But I'm watching him. Oh yes, I'm watching him like a hawk watches a... well, like a hawk watches something suspicious.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, Doily Manor at last! What a magnificently decrepit establishment — reminds me of my summer home, only considerably less grand, naturally. Now then, let us see what secrets this dusty old pile is hiding. I do believe I shall consult the guest book — purely out of aristocratic courtesy, you understand. Nothing to do with treasure hunting. Not in the slightest.

The FOOLS! They're all just standing about gawping at the chandelier while I, Reginald Foxworth, begin my systematic plundering of this manor's secrets! That guest book could contain the names of previous visitors — and more importantly, any CLUES they may have scribbled about the treasure's location. And once I've gleaned what I need, I shall send these buffoons off on a wild goose chase to the kitchen while I investigate that MOST promising library inscription. The fake medal in my pocket will come in handy too — perhaps I can convince one of these simpletons that I'm an official treasure inspector with full authority to confiscate all findings. Oh, Reginald, you magnificent devil!

Peter Perfect: What a splendid, if somewhat precarious, establishment! That chandelier alone could flatten a lesser man — but James Hartwell is not a lesser man. Now then, let us see who has signed the guest book. A thorough reconnaissance is the foundation of every great endeavour — and I intend to be *very* thorough indeed.

Clara isn't here. My heart sinks — but only for a moment. She must be deeper in the manor. I'll sign the guest book with a flourish, examine it for clues, and then search every room until I find her. When I do, I shall be mid-adventure, looking every inch the hero. That's the plan. An elaborate plan, yes, but thoroughness is my hallmark.

I just love a good library clue! And Professor Pat Pending looks like the cleverest person in the room — if anyone can help me decipher an inscription, it's him. Dick Dastardly keeps giving Sneekly these funny little looks, but I'm sure they're just old friends catching up. Nothing suspicious about that at all!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, splendid, splendid — everyone's signed in, most proper! Now then, if you'll all excuse me for just a moment, I must attend to a few matters in the Library. Dreadfully dusty in there, I'm afraid — wouldn't want any of our distinguished guests to suffer an unfortunate... *ahem*... allergic reaction. Do feel free to explore at your leisure! The manor is yours, though I would advise against touching the chandelier. It has a rather temperamental disposition.

Perfect — while these fools mill about examining coat racks and signing guest books, I shall reconnoitre the Library! That inscription on the mantelpiece could be a clue to the Diamond, and those towering bookshelves... oh, the POSSIBILITIES! Every great villain needs a properly dramatic setting for their scheme, and what could be more dramatic than a shadowy library full of precarious literary hazards? I must find Clara's likely path through the manor and prepare something SPECTACULARLY elaborate along the way. A simple trap? Never! Vincent Marsh does not DO simple. We're talking tripwires, counterweights, and at LEAST one red herring!

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi, lads, look at that coat rack! It's wobblier than Clinger after three pints at the Dog and Duck! That thing's a DEATH TRAP, that is! One gust of wind, one careless elbow, and WHAM — someone's getting a face full of Victorian timber! And who's it gonna fall on? Some innocent person, that's who! Right, Danny's on it. I'm gonna give it a proper inspection before anyone gets hurt. Stand back, everyone — this is a job for a professional!

See, this is what people don't understand about protection work. It ain't all car chases and daring rescues. Sometimes it's about noticing the wobbly coat rack before it notices you. That Sneekly bloke probably left it there on purpose, knowing him. Not that I'm accusing nobody of nothing. But if that coat rack 'accidentally' fell on Clara... well. Danny don't believe in coincidences, that's all I'm saying.

Dick Dastardly: I say — did anyone else notice that rather FASCINATING entry in the guest book? Third page, cramped handwriting — a certain Lord Doily himself noted that the family treasure was secured in a place of GREAT HEAT. 'Where the flames dance and copper gleams,' I believe were his exact words. Now, I'm no detective, but that sounds REMARKABLY like a kitchen to me — wood-burning stove, copper pots, you see? I suggest you all investigate the kitchen POST-HASTE while I... er... keep watch here. Guard the entrance. Terribly important job, guarding the entrance. Someone has to do it.

MWAHAHAHA! There was no such entry in the guest book, of course — I made the whole thing up! 'Where the flames dance and copper gleams' — oh, Reginald, you poetic GENIUS! While these credulous fools tear the kitchen apart looking for treasure hidden in a stove that doesn't exist, I shall saunter casually into the library and examine that MOST intriguing mantelpiece inscription. The Doily Diamond is practically MINE already! I can feel the weight of it in my pocket! The sheer, unparalleled BRILLIANCE of my scheming knows no bounds!
Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

She's here! Clara Bellingham, in the flesh, and looking every bit as magnificent as I'd imagined. Right then, Hartwell — this is your moment. Lead the expedition to the library, discover that inscription, crack the code, find the treasure, and look devastatingly heroic doing it. Simple. Well, not simple — I've already mentally catalogued seventeen possible contingencies including structural collapse, rival treasure hunters, and the possibility that the inscription is in Latin, which I can mostly read if I squint. But the core plan is sound. To the library!
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the coat-rack.
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh, would you just LOOK at this magnificent mantelpiece, y'all! There's a riddle carved right into the stone — how perfectly THRILLING! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Well now, I do declare, my grandmother used to read me riddles just like this one back in Mobile! And unless my memory is playing tricks on me — which it NEVER does when it comes to puzzles — the answer is a MAP! A map has all those things drawn on it without any of the real things! Oh, I just KNEW this library would be full of clues! Stand back, everyone — let me see if this clever little mantelpiece has a secret to share with us!

I do hope solving this riddle leads somewhere wonderful! And isn't it just the sweetest thing that Sneekly rushed right over to make sure we're all settled in? Such a dedicated estate manager. Though I can't help but notice he and Dick Dastardly keep exchanging the most peculiar glances... but I'm sure it's nothing. Probably just admiring each other's fashion sense!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, welcome, welcome to the Library, everyone! Do mind the dust — Lord Doily was rather more fond of COLLECTING books than READING them, I'm afraid. Now then, I see you've all noticed the old mantelpiece there. Quite the curiosity, that inscription. Lord Doily was terribly fond of riddles — said they kept the mind sharp and the servants confused. I've dusted around it a thousand times but never could make heads or tails of it myself. Cities without houses, forests without trees... dreadfully perplexing! Perhaps one of you clever guests might have a go?

Oh, I know PRECISELY what the answer is — a MAP! But let them puzzle over it while I watch who's clever enough to be dangerous. If Clara solves it first, she'll be one step closer to the Diamond... and I'll need to ensure her next step leads somewhere considerably more PERILOUS. These bookshelves are practically BEGGING to be weaponised. And did I mention how MAGNIFICENTLY heavy leather-bound volumes are when dropped from a great height?
The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with sergeant-blast.

See, this is the thing about Danny — thorough to a fault, some might say. I've just spent valuable protection time inspecting a coat rack while Clara's wandered into a room with a bloke called 'The Hooded Claw.' THE HOODED CLAW. I mean, I ain't accusing nobody of nothing, but that ain't exactly a name that screams 'trustworthy estate agent,' is it? And now Dastardly's in there too, after that whole performance about the kitchen. Something stinks worse than Clinger's lockup after curry night. I need to get in that library before someone 'accidentally' drops a bookshelf on our girl.

Dick Dastardly: Ah-HA! How FORTUITOUS that we've all gathered in the library! I couldn't help but notice this inscription on the mantelpiece — 'cities but no houses, forests but no trees' — and as a distinguished scholar and holder of the Order of the Golden Quill — *adjusts fake medal* — I can tell you with ABSOLUTE CERTAINTY that the answer is A BOOK! Cities in chapters, forests in descriptions, water in prose! It's OBVIOUSLY referring to one of these volumes on the shelves! I suggest you all begin searching — there must be THOUSANDS of books here, and the treasure clue is surely tucked inside one of them! Every spine, every page! Leave NO book unturned! I shall just... lean here against the mantelpiece... supervising.

MWAHAHAHA! A BOOK! What utter DRIVEL I've just spouted — cities in CHAPTERS?! The answer is a MAP, you fools! A MAP! And while these gullible dimwits pull every mouldering tome off the shelves searching for a clue that doesn't exist, I, the INCOMPARABLE Reginald Foxworth, shall whisper the TRUE answer to the mantelpiece and claim whatever secret it conceals! Oh, I am WASTED on this century — I should have been a Renaissance schemer! The Borgias would have WEPT with envy!
Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

My heart is hammering like a steam engine. If I'm right about this riddle, and the mantelpiece reveals something — a hidden compartment, a secret map — Clara will see me as the dashing intellectual adventurer I've always aspired to be. And if I'm wrong... well, I'll look like a man who confidently announced the wrong answer to a stone fireplace in front of the woman he's trying to impress. So let's hope I'm not wrong.

I am POSITIVELY vibrating with excitement! Peter and I both solved the riddle — we make quite the team! Though I can't help but notice Dick Dastardly was trying awfully hard to get everyone searching through thousands of books while he leaned against the mantelpiece. Almost as if he wanted to keep us all busy and distracted... but no, no, I'm sure he was just enthusiastic about literature! And Sneekly examining the bookshelves right after we solved the riddle — just being a thorough host, naturally!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with peter-perfect.

Upside-down books on the shelves — that's a CLUE, and I spotted it first! But I can't just yank them out with everyone watching. So instead, I'll make a grand show of 'tidying' while actually cataloguing their positions. And Peter Perfect WHISPERING to Clara about maps? Oh, you noble, chiselled NUISANCE. Every answer you hand her brings her closer to the Diamond and further from safety. I need to separate them. Perhaps... yes, perhaps I could suggest the gentlemen investigate the Laboratory while the ladies rest in the reading chairs? No — too obvious. Clara would see right through it. I need something more ELABORATE. Something involving counterweights, perhaps, or a strategically placed volume of encyclopaedias...

The Ant Hill Mob: OI OI! Nobody panic, the cavalry's arrived! Clara — Miss Bellingham — don't you move a MUSCLE, darlin'! I've been doing a thorough security sweep of this gaff and I don't mind telling you, the structural integrity is SHOCKING. That coat rack in the hall? Wobblier than a jelly on a skateboard. And now THIS lot — bookshelves leaning like they've had six pints, mysterious riddles carved into stone, and everyone solving puzzles without a proper RISK ASSESSMENT! Stand aside, stand aside — let me just check these shelves ain't about to come down on someone's head before anyone goes pulling levers or pressing ancient mechanisms!

Look at Sneekly over there, cool as a cucumber while Peter Perfect plays Indiana Jones with the fireplace. A man called 'The Hooded Claw' who ain't bothered by secret mechanisms going off? That's either very brave or very prepared. And I don't reckon he's the brave type. I need to get between them shelves and Clara before whatever happens next.

Dick Dastardly: Well, THAT was thoroughly underwhelming! The mantelpiece is nothing but a bit of decorative stonework — no hidden compartments, no secret levers, no treasure whatsoever! I TOLD you all the answer was in the BOOKS! But did anyone listen to the holder of the Order of the Golden Quill? NO! You were all too busy crowding around a perfectly ordinary fireplace! Now then, since I've CONCLUSIVELY proven the mantelpiece is a dead end, I shall graciously demonstrate the CORRECT approach by examining these bookshelves myself. Stand aside!

CURSES! Peter Perfect got to the mantelpiece before me — that square-jawed SIMPLETON may have found the next clue! But ALL IS NOT LOST! The riddle says MAP, and maps are kept in BOOKS, and books are kept on SHELVES! If there's a secret map hidden among these volumes, Reginald Foxworth shall find it FIRST! I just need to search the shelves before anyone else thinks to look there — which, thanks to my BRILLIANT earlier misdirection about books, they'll think I'm simply following my own bad advice! REVERSE PSYCHOLOGY AT ITS FINEST! Oh, I am a GENIUS of such staggering proportions!

Peter Perfect: Ladies and gentlemen — and I use that term loosely for some present — the answer to this riddle is unmistakably A MAP! Cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish — these are all features one finds drawn upon a cartographer's work! Now, Dick, old boy, I appreciate your enthusiasm for literature, but I'm afraid 'a book' is quite wide of the mark. A book about cities would still DESCRIBE houses. A map merely REPRESENTS the city — no houses required! I've just had my hands all over this magnificent stonework, and I believe this mantelpiece is trying to tell us something rather more specific. There may be a hidden compartment — a secret map tucked away by Lord Doily himself! Allow me to take a closer look at the craftsmanship here. Stand back, everyone — particularly you, Miss Bellingham. These old mechanisms can be unpredictable, and I wouldn't dream of letting any flying debris so much as graze your sleeve!

My hands are trembling slightly. Not from fear — from the absolutely electric possibility that I'm about to discover a hidden treasure map in front of Clara Bellingham. I've already mentally prepared contingency plans for: the compartment being stuck (I'll use measured force), the compartment releasing a cloud of centuries-old dust (I'll shield Clara with my jacket), or the compartment containing something disappointing like a dead spider (I'll pretend it's a fascinating archaeological specimen). I've also noticed that Sneekly positioned himself near the bookshelves rather suspiciously quickly. And Dastardly is LEANING against the mantelpiece — is he trying to block something? No, no — benefit of the doubt, James. Benefit of the doubt.

Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Why, I do declare — everyone hush for just one teeny tiny moment! The answer to this riddle is as clear as a Georgia sunrise on a summer mornin'! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — that's a MAP, y'all! A map has all those things drawn right on it without a single real house or tree or little fishy in sight! Now, Dick Dastardly, sugar, bless your heart for suggestin' books, but a book about a city would DESCRIBE the houses in it, wouldn't it? A map just shows the city as a dot! Peter and I figured this out together — we make quite the detective duo, if I do say so myself! Now let me just give this gorgeous old mantelpiece the answer it's been waitin' a hundred years to hear!

Oh my stars, my heart is just POUNDIN' with anticipation! What if the mantelpiece opens up and there's a treasure map inside leadin' straight to the Doily Diamond? I am BESIDE myself with excitement! And isn't it just the sweetest thing how Peter keeps tryin' to protect me from flying debris? Though I can handle a little dust, thank you very much!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, yes, yes — a MAP, of course! How delightfully clever of Lord Doily. *adjusts spectacles nervously* Now, while you all examine the mantelpiece — and DO be careful with it, that stonework is FRIGHTFULLY old — I shall just attend to these bookshelves. Several volumes appear to have been shelved incorrectly, you see. Spines facing the wrong direction! Most irregular. Lord Doily was EXCEPTIONALLY particular about his library. If I don't set them right, I shall never forgive myself. Estate manager's duty and all that, hm hm!

While these FOOLS congratulate each other on solving a children's riddle, I — Vincent Marsh, the HOODED CLAW — shall decode the REAL secret of this library! Those upside-down books are speaking to me, and I intend to listen! And once I know where the Diamond truly lies... well, Clara Bellingham's treasure hunt will come to a most THEATRICAL conclusion. Something involving a collapsing bookshelf, perhaps? Or a secret passage that leads somewhere DELICIOUSLY dangerous? The possibilities make my villainous heart SING!

The Ant Hill Mob: HOLD IT, HOLD IT, HOLD IT! Nobody touch NOTHING else! Miss Bellingham, you said something SHIFTED in that mantelpiece? SHIFTED?! Do you have ANY idea what that means? That means there's a MECHANISM in there — counterweights, pulleys, possibly even a Victorian booby trap! Lord Doily was clearly off his nut, God rest him, and I ain't having our Clara standing next to an unstable load-bearing puzzle box without a proper structural survey! Stand back, darlin' — let Danny handle this. I've got experience with unstable structures. Me nan's shed collapsed three times and I rebuilt it every time. Well, twice. The third time we just put a tarp over it. BUT THE POINT STANDS! Let me just give this inscription a proper feel — check for loose stones, hidden switches, anything that might go BANG in the night...

Look at Sneekly watching me from them shelves. Cool as you like, ain't he? Not a flicker of worry about ancient mechanisms going off. Either he knows it's harmless because he's already been through it, or he knows exactly what it does and he WANTS it to go off. Either way, if I'm standing between Clara and whatever this mantelpiece is connected to, at least she's covered. The lads are counting on me. Clinger, Dum-Dum, Zippy — they'd all say the same thing: 'Danny, get your oversized head in front of the danger.' And that's exactly what I'm doing.

Dick Dastardly: I say, how FASCINATING — these bookshelves are in absolutely DREADFUL condition! Books upside down, spines cracked — it's an OUTRAGE against literature! As holder of the Order of the Golden Quill, I simply CANNOT abide such bibliographic vandalism! Allow me to set things right — a gentleman ALWAYS tidies a disordered shelf! Oh, and speaking of disorder — Slag brothers, I couldn't help but notice a rather PECULIAR bubbling sound coming from the Laboratory just through there. Sounded rather like liquid gold being heated in a crucible, if you ask me. Might be worth investigating, what? Could be TERRIBLY valuable!

MWAHAHAHA! The upside-down books — of COURSE! Every villain worth his monocle knows that in a manor library, upside-down books are ALWAYS the key to a hidden mechanism! While I send those boulder-brained Slag brothers off to chase phantom gold in the Laboratory, I shall pull these inverted volumes and reveal whatever secret Lord Doily has hidden here! The map to the Doily Diamond is practically in my GRASP! Oh, Reginald, you magnificent, scheming MARVEL — your cunning is exceeded only by your impeccable taste in waistcoats!
Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

My heart is absolutely HAMMERING. If this works — if I crack open a secret compartment in front of Clara — I shall dine on this story for YEARS. And if the whole mantelpiece collapses? Well, I've already calculated the optimal angle to throw myself between the falling stonework and Clara. Either way, I come out looking rather good.

The Ant Hill Mob interacted with the mantelpiece.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh, Peter, you absolute DARLIN'! You are just the most chivalrous man I have ever had the pleasure of solvin' a riddle alongside! And Danny, sugar, I do appreciate your concern about booby traps — your nan's shed experience is clearly invaluable in situations like these! But y'all — LOOK! We both touched this mantelpiece after sayin' the answer was a MAP, and I do believe somethin' may have SHIFTED in the stonework! My heart is beatin' faster than a hummingbird's wings at a honeysuckle bush! Let me take a closer look at this gorgeous old carving and see if Lord Doily left us a little surprise! Oh, I just KNEW this adventure was gonna be absolutely DIVINE!

If there IS a secret compartment in this mantelpiece, it could lead straight to the Doily Diamond! I am SO close I can practically feel those facets sparklin' against my fingertips! Though I do wonder why Dick keeps tryin' to send everyone away from this spot... probably just his competitive nature, bless his schemin' little heart.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.

Get AWAY from my bookshelves, you moustache-twirling buffoon! Those upside-down books are MINE to decode! Every second Dastardly spends hovering near this shelf is a second I cannot work my magic unobserved. And over there, Peter Perfect is about to crack open the mantelpiece like a Christmas cracker — if there's a map inside, Clara will have a direct path to the Diamond! I need to find the REAL hiding place first, or at the very least discover a secret passage I can use to stage something DEVASTATINGLY theatrical along her route. Oh, the FRUSTRATION! Surrounded by competitors on all sides! But Vincent Marsh does not panic. Vincent Marsh SCHEMES!

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi, oi, OI! Right, I've given that mantelpiece a thorough going-over — proper professional job, thank you very much — and I can confirm there is DEFINITELY mechanical components in there. Counterweights, sliding stones, the works. Victorian engineering at its most DANGEROUS. Now, Peter, mate, you crack on with your puzzle solving, but keep Clara — Miss Bellingham — at arm's length from any moving parts, yeah? Meanwhile, I can't help but NOTICE that our esteemed estate manager AND the distinguished holder of the Golden Quill have BOTH decided that NOW is the perfect time for a bit of shelf tidying. At the SAME TIME. In the SAME library. With the SAME bookshelves. Funny, that. Not suspicious AT ALL. So if nobody minds, I'm just gonna mosey on over and have a look at what's so FASCINATING about these upside-down books. Structural safety purposes only, of course. Can't have shelves toppling onto inheritance beneficiaries, can we?

Two of 'em at the shelves. TWO. I ain't got the brains to work out exactly what they're planning, but I've got enough sense to know that when two dodgy geezers are both drawn to the same spot like magnets to a fridge, something's hidden there that they both want. And whatever it is, it ain't gonna fall on Clara's head. Not on Danny's watch.

Dick Dastardly: Yes, yes, a MAP — I knew that AGES ago, of course! I was merely testing you all to see if ANYONE in this room possessed even a FRACTION of my intellectual prowess! I see Perfect has already fumbled about with the mantelpiece — allow ME to show you how a REAL gentleman of letters handles an antique puzzle mechanism! I have EXTENSIVE experience with Victorian secret compartments — the Order of the Golden Quill requires a full semester on architectural concealment devices!

CURSES! The bookshelves were a complete DUD — not a single hidden lever, secret panel, or spring-loaded mechanism among the lot! Just BOOKS! Meanwhile that chrome-plated charlatan Peter Perfect has his hands all over MY mantelpiece! MY treasure clue! If he's found a map to the Doily Diamond before me, I shall NEVER forgive myself! I must elbow my way in there and take credit for whatever he's discovered — or better yet, misdirect everyone about what it MEANS!

Peter Perfect: The answer is a MAP! Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — it can ONLY be a map! And Penelope was absolutely right — do you FEEL that? The stone is shifting! There's a mechanism built right into this mantelpiece — Lord Doily, you magnificent old fox! Everyone stand back — Clara, stay behind me, if you please. I've prepared for exactly this contingency. Contingency seven, in fact: 'hidden spring-loaded compartment triggered by correct riddle answer.' I've braced my stance at precisely the right angle to shield anyone nearby from flying masonry, loose mortar, or — in the unlikely event — a small burst of Victorian-era pressurised gas. Which I HAVE read about. They were surprisingly common in manor houses of this period. Now then — let's see what Lord Doily left for us!

My hands are trembling with excitement but I'm channelling it into looking purposeful rather than nervous. If something magnificent slides open in front of Clara, I shall be the hero of the hour. If the whole thing crumbles, I shall be the man who threw himself between her and danger. I genuinely cannot lose here. Well — I COULD lose if nothing happens at all and I look like an overdramatic fool. That would be contingency eighteen, which I had rather hoped to avoid.

The Ant Hill Mob examined the bookshelves.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh, PETER! Dick! Y'all stand back just a SMIDGE, sugar — I felt that shift in the stone earlier and I believe this mantelpiece wants to be ACTIVATED, not just admired! Danny confirmed there are counterweights and slidin' stones built right into this gorgeous old thing — Lord Doily was an ABSOLUTE genius of Victorian engineerin'! Now, the answer to the riddle is A MAP — we ALL know that — so let me just press right HERE where the inscription ends and see if this clever old mechanism does what I THINK it's gonna do! Oh my stars and GARTERS, if there's a secret compartment with a clue to the Doily Diamond hidden in this very mantelpiece, I may just FAINT from sheer delight! Though I promise I will faint GRACEFULLY and only AFTER I've secured whatever's inside!

My heart is absolutely RACIN'! If this mantelpiece opens up, it could be the biggest clue yet! And I do notice that Dick Dastardly suddenly wants to be RIGHT here at the mantelpiece after tryin' to send everyone away to the kitchen and the laboratory... but I'm sure he's just excited about the discovery like the rest of us!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, oh dear — do be CAREFUL with that stonework, everyone! The mortar in these old mantelpieces is frightfully temperamental. I really must insist — but never mind, never mind, you're all clearly quite determined. While you attend to that, I shall just have a look at these reading chairs. Dreadfully dusty, I'm afraid — the previous housekeeper let things go rather shockingly. I do hope none of Lord Doily's upholstery has been damaged by the damp. One must maintain STANDARDS, even in a house of mysteries!

Let them have their precious mantelpiece! Every eye in the room is fixed on Peter's little strongman performance. PERFECT. While they gawp at shifting stones, Vincent Marsh shall search these chairs with the thoroughness of a man whose LIFE depends on staying one step ahead. And if I find a secret passage or a hidden compartment... well. That knowledge stays with ME. A map is useless if the person holding it never reaches the destination, and I have SUCH elaborate plans for dear Clara's journey!

The Ant Hill Mob: Right, right, right — everyone's all excited about the mantelpiece, and fair enough, it's a lovely bit of stonework, very atmospheric. But has ANYONE stopped to wonder WHY half these books are upside down? Not ME, obviously, I noticed STRAIGHT AWAY on account of being naturally observant.
